stories.title: Supreme court rules 24-hour arrest rule starts from detention
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the 24-hour window for producing an individual before a magistrate begins the moment detention starts, rather than at formal arrest. The court held that fundamental rights to liberty apply regardless of whether an arrest is officially recorded. Time is now officially moving.

stories.title: Supreme court bars illegal detention as lawyers cite emergency
stories.summary: The Supreme Court held an extraordinary Sunday hearing to order the government and Delhi Police to cease mass detentions and restore movement. The bench issued notices to the Union Home Secretary and Delhi Police Commissioner after lawyers compared the recent clampdown to the 1975 Emergency period.

stories.title: Supreme court ends distinction between detention and arrest
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that law enforcement cannot circumvent constitutional protections by delaying formal arrests. The mandatory 24-hour period for magistrate production now begins the moment liberty is curtailed. The court clarified that the deadline is sacrosanct, even for those held for search and seizure purposes.

stories.title: Supreme court seeks response on election commissioner immunity
stories.summary: The Supreme Court asked the Centre and the Election Commission to respond to a petition challenging the legal immunity granted to election commissioners. The plea argues that the 2023 law places commissioners above the law and violates the constitutional framework. The court is currently reviewing the matter.

stories.title: Supreme court calls for review of two-child election norms
stories.summary: The Supreme Court suggested a fresh look at laws disqualifying people with more than two children from local elections. Citing a fertility rate of 1.9, the court noted that population-control rationales have lost relevance. India is now facing the prospect of an ageing population instead of overpopulation.

stories.title: Supreme court refuses bail for Azam Khan in ED case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court declined to hear a bail plea from Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan regarding a new Enforcement Directorate case. The court transferred the matter to the Allahabad High Court, ordering it to be listed before a division bench by November 16. The legal process continues.

stories.title: Amit Shah challenges Rahul Gandhi to parliamentary debate
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah challenged Rahul Gandhi to debate allegations inside Parliament rather than on the streets. Shah claimed the Congress leader would run away from a formal response. The government maintains that Parliament remains the supreme forum for democratic discussion and substantive policy debate.

stories.title: Amit Shah criticises Congress for disrupting parliament
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah accused Rahul Gandhi of avoiding substantive issues and turning walkouts into a political culture. Shah asserted that Parliament is the supreme forum for debate and criticised the opposition for taking confrontations to the streets. The government remains focused on parliamentary proceedings.

stories.title: Congress says fight is to restore democracy
stories.summary: Congress general secretary KC Venugopal stated the party's goal is to restore democracy rather than just form a government. Amid protests against the Election Commission, Venugopal claimed the Centre is turning institutions into tools for anti-democratic actions. The party continues to advocate for its leadership.

stories.title: Youth Congress suspends 200 members for skipping rally
stories.summary: The Indian Youth Congress suspended over 200 office-bearers across seven states for failing to attend the INDIA bloc rally on November 1. The rally featured senior opposition leaders who accused the BJP and Election Commission of undermining democratic institutions. Attendance is now a matter of internal discipline.

stories.title: Two dead in Chawri Bazar building collapse
stories.summary: Two people died after an under-construction building collapsed in Old Delhi on Thursday. The Delhi Chief Minister ordered the suspension of two municipal engineers and an FIR against the contractor. Officials stated that those responsible for the safety failure will not be spared by the authorities.

stories.title: Two dead in Delhi building collapse
stories.summary: A three-storey under-construction building collapsed near Chawri Bazar Metro Station on Thursday morning, killing two people. Rescue operations are currently underway to clear the debris. Local authorities confirmed that four others were rushed to the hospital by residents before emergency services arrived at the site.

stories.title: Building collapse in Delhi
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Two people are confirmed dead following a three-storey building collapse in the Chawri Bazaar area of Delhi. Rescue operations are ongoing as authorities work to clear the site and investigate the cause of the structural failure.

stories.title: Three killed in Jharkhand coal pile collapse
stories.summary: Three women were killed and three others injured when a coal heap collapsed at the Kathara colliery on Thursday. The victims were collecting coal when the pile gave way. Local police confirmed the incident occurred early in the morning under the jurisdiction of the Kathara outpost.

stories.title: Businessman killed in police encounter
stories.summary: A businessman accused of murdering five people at a hotel last week was killed in a police encounter on Wednesday. Police stated he was shot while attempting to escape custody during a transfer to Sibsagar. The suspect had been involved in a dispute over the hotel lease.

stories.title: Man dies after fall from Gurugram balcony
stories.summary: A 28-year-old man died after falling from the tenth floor of a residential society in Gurugram on Wednesday. Security guards discovered the body after hearing a loud thud. The victim was the son of a senior Border Security Force official. Police are investigating the circumstances of the fall.

stories.title: Ex-India hockey captain MM Somaya says 1980 Olympic Gold stolen in Bengaluru home burglary
stories.summary: Ex-India hockey captain MM Somaya says 1980 Olympic Gold stolen in Bengaluru home burglary The gold medal, which MM Somaya won as part of the Indian team at the Moscow Olympics, was stolen along with three other international sporting medals. Former India hockey captain M

stories.title: Three killed in Manipur gunfight
stories.summary: Three people were killed in an exchange of gunfire between suspected militant factions in Manipur’s Noney district on Wednesday. Police recovered the bodies following the clash, which reportedly involved the NSCN-IM and ZUF-J groups. Post-mortem examinations were conducted at the local community health centre.

stories.title: Mahadev betting app co-founder arrested in Dubai
stories.summary: Ravi Uppal, co-founder of the Mahadev online betting app, has been arrested in Dubai. Officials termed the arrest a major breakthrough in the multi-crore illegal betting case. The development follows the extradition of his business partner, Sourabh Chandrakar, from Oman earlier this week.

stories.title: Mahadev co-founder Uppal held in Dubai
stories.summary: Ravi Uppal, co-founder of the Mahadev online betting app and a key accused in an illegal betting case, has been arrested in Dubai. Officials described the arrest as a major breakthrough. It follows the recent extradition of his business partner from Oman.

stories.title: StartupTN reports over 50% of startups led by women
stories.summary: StartupTN Chairman Singai G. Ramachandran stated that 50.8% of the 16,000 registered startups in Tamil Nadu are led by women. He noted that the state must move beyond simple hiring to create infrastructure specifically designed for women, as current mindsets regarding gender roles remain entrenched.

stories.title: SRMIST to open SRMJEE applications in November
stories.summary: SRM Institute of Science and Technology will open applications for its joint entrance examination on November 4. The exam covers engineering, medicine, law, and other programmes across 160 centres. The first phase of engineering tests is scheduled for April 17 and 18, 2027.

stories.title: SRM University-AP tops state rankings
stories.summary: SRM University-AP has secured the top position among universities in Andhra Pradesh in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027. The institution also placed among the top 51 universities in India. This marks the university's debut in the international ranking framework.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh releases teacher recruitment notification
stories.summary: The Andhra Pradesh School Education Department has issued a notification for 2,721 teacher posts. Applications for the recruitment test will be accepted from November 11 to November 30. The vacancies include regular teaching roles, special education positions, and openings in various educational societies.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu releases three-year battery storage policy
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu has launched a policy targeting 2.5 GW of battery energy storage by 2029. New solar projects of one MW and above commissioned after April 1, 2027, will be required to install storage capacity equal to at least 10% of their total output.

stories.title: TNCCF cancels onion orders over quality concerns
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Cooperative Consumer Federation cancelled orders for 400 tonnes of onions, citing that the vegetables failed to meet quality criteria including a 45 mm minimum radius. The federation clarified that the rotten stock found at a railway shed belonged to NAFED.

stories.title: Tasmac staff report challenges with bottle buyback
stories.summary: Tasmac employees have returned to work, but the mandatory bottle buyback scheme is causing operational friction. Salesmen report technical glitches and customers attempting to return discarded bottles found near shops for refunds. Staff have requested that the government impose a limit on returns.

stories.title: Tasmac introduces bottle buyback scheme
stories.summary: Tasmac has introduced a 10 rupee increase in liquor prices alongside a bottle buyback scheme. The move follows government efforts to stop employees from charging above the maximum retail price, a practice staff previously used to cover miscellaneous expenses like bottle breakages and internet charges.

stories.title: Study links cyclone damage to climate change
stories.summary: A study from Imperial College London suggests that climate change increased the damage caused by Cyclone Arnab by 33%. Researchers used the Imperial College Storm Model to compare the October 28 event against a pre-industrial baseline. The storm produced winds of 202 kilometres per hour.

stories.title: Residents report green water in Erode district
stories.summary: Residents and farmers in Erode district have reported that the Cauvery river has turned green, prompting fears of industrial pollution. Locals claim the water causes itching and is unfit for use. Authorities have not yet identified the source of the suspected chemical effluents.

stories.title: Delhi government increases pollution enforcement
stories.summary: The Delhi government has inspected 1,232 construction sites, finding violations at 203 locations. Authorities imposed 59.15 lakh rupees in environmental compensation during the first four days of winter restrictions. On Wednesday alone, 77 sites were flagged for failing to follow construction norms.

stories.title: Draft policy warns of high cost for sustainable aviation fuel
stories.summary: A draft policy from the Centre suggests that sustainable aviation fuel could cost two to three times more than conventional jet fuel. The government is proposing financial incentives to encourage production as it prepares to introduce mandatory blending requirements for domestic airlines.

stories.title: Gurugram residents report open burning of scrap
stories.summary: A resident group has written to pollution authorities regarding the recurring practice of burning metal filters and scrap materials in Gurugram. The group, CleanAirBharat, is calling for coordinated enforcement and systemic responses to curb the burning of industrial waste in residential areas.

stories.title: Activist demands transparency for data centre project
stories.summary: Environmental activist Rajendra Singh has demanded that the state government disclose all environmental and land-use permissions for a proposed hyperscale data centre near Visakhapatnam. He urged officials to ensure the project complies with laws protecting the nearby Kambalakonda eco-sensitive zone.

stories.title: Conservationists warn against restoration of historic mosque
stories.summary: Conservationists have expressed concern over the restoration of the 17th-century Malshahi Masjid in Kashmir. While the government has allocated 5.01 crore rupees for the project, experts warn that current construction activities, including stone paving, could erase historical layers from the Mughal era.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu initiates conservation plan for foxes and jackals
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has begun a conservation plan for Bengal foxes and golden jackals. The initiative, first announced in the 2025 budget, aims to protect the species to maintain ecological balance across the state's diverse habitats, ranging from coastal plains to mountainous terrain.

stories.title: Southern India has grown wetter over seven decades
stories.summary: Southern India has become wetter over the past seven decades, according to an IMD and IITM study. The area classified as hot semi-arid has nearly halved, with much of the region transitioning to a tropical savannah climate. The peninsula is now three-fourths savannah, up from three-fifths.

stories.title: Powerball jackpots reach record heights
stories.summary: Two back-to-back Powerball jackpots now rank among the ten largest in history, following an $847 million win in New Jersey. Stephen Durrell of the Powerball Product Group called the run a testament to the excitement the game generates. The lottery continues to celebrate life-changing wins.

stories.title: Trump party suffers midterm losses
stories.summary: US voters angered by rising living costs have handed Democrats control of Congress. Analysts suggest the political humbling may force Trump to be more cautious regarding trade truces with Beijing. China now has space to fortify its trade ties before a potentially less friendly administration takes power.

stories.title: Arab parties consider alliance to unseat Netanyahu
stories.summary: A veteran Arab lawmaker says his bloc is willing to break precedent to join Jewish-led parties in removing Benjamin Netanyahu. The partnership remains politically fraught, as the Joint List would be backing a government unlikely to curb settlement expansion or end ongoing wars in the region.

stories.title: Sergio Gor considered for senior promotion
stories.summary: Following Republican losses in the midterms, internal discussions suggest US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor is a contender for a senior promotion. Sources familiar with the matter report that Gor, a close ally of Donald Trump, has been laying the groundwork for an expanded role.

stories.title: Trump defends Hegseth despite election losses
stories.summary: Asked if he would replace Pete Hegseth, Trump told reporters he thinks he is doing a very good job. While some advisers suggest Hegseth could be on the chopping block due to war-related discontent, others note that someone will eventually be blamed for the losses.

stories.title: Hasina maintains plan to return to Bangladesh
stories.summary: Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina says she does not need foreign backing to return to Bangladesh. Despite being sentenced to death in absentia for a crackdown on protesters, her plan to leave exile in India by December remains unchanged. She expects no pressure from the US or India.

stories.title: Foreign Secretary discusses cooperation with Nepal
stories.summary: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met with Nepalese officials in Kathmandu to discuss bilateral cooperation and development projects. The talks served as preparations for Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India later this month. Cooperation remains the stated priority for both nations.

stories.title: Sheikh Hasina reiterates return to Bangladesh
stories.summary: Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has confirmed she will return to Bangladesh in December despite a death sentence. She told The Associated Press that if death is her destiny, she would rather face it among her own people. She has been in exile since 2024.

stories.title: India and Israel oppose arms control resolution
stories.summary: India and Israel voted against a Pakistan-sponsored UN resolution on conventional arms control. Sources dismissed claims of diplomatic coordination, noting that the shared vote reflects a lack of nuanced understanding. New Delhi maintains that security concerns extend beyond the sub-regional boundaries defined by the resolution.

stories.title: UK launches AI Biosecurity Lab
stories.summary: The UK has established an AI Biosecurity Lab to accelerate medical research while preventing the use of AI in building biological weapons. Backed by £100 million in government funding, the lab aims to separate breakthroughs from risks. The race to secure the technology has officially begun.

stories.title: Cert-In mandates AI security audits
stories.summary: Cert-In has issued guidelines requiring organisations to conduct regular security assessments for AI systems. The 107-page framework applies to all entities developing or deploying AI in India, including foreign firms handling local data. Compliance requirements apply uniformly, with no exemptions for smaller startups.

stories.title: Cert-In warns of AI-driven financial attacks
stories.summary: Cert-In and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre have warned financial firms of AI-driven cyberattacks leading to unauthorised fund transfers. Hackers are reportedly using AI agents to exploit payment systems. The stolen money is moved through mule accounts before being withdrawn via IMPS and NEFT.

stories.title: Potash explosives emerge as firework alternative
stories.summary: AIIMS Delhi reports a rise in burn injuries caused by homemade explosives using potassium nitrate and sulphur. Doctors have called for preventive measures as these mixtures become an alternative to conventional firecrackers. The data shows an emerging threat from the use of potash during festivals.

stories.title: Delhi Police files FIR against Meta
stories.summary: Delhi Police has registered an FIR against Meta India regarding the availability of child sexual abuse material on its platforms. The National Human Rights Commission directed the action following concerns over online advertisements. Meta claims predators are increasingly using ads to evade detection.

stories.title: UN celebrates Keralam poverty reduction
stories.summary: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights released an animated video to mark the 40th anniversary of the UN Declaration on the Right to Development. The video celebrates Keralam declaring itself free from extreme poverty, a status the state announced in November 2025 following a five-year process.

stories.title: Keralam moves to build oceanarium
stories.summary: The state cabinet has approved the formation of a special purpose vehicle to develop an International Maritime Museum and Oceanarium. The project is billed as the most advanced in the country and is expected to boost tourism. The entity will initially operate as a Section 8 company.

stories.title: Experts warn of marine ecosystem threats
stories.summary: Marine scientists meeting at a CMFRI symposium warned that warming seas, coral bleaching, and unpredictable ocean conditions are challenging fisheries and coastal livelihoods. Around 300 participants from 30 countries discussed the need for integrated monitoring to manage these rapidly changing conditions in the face of mounting climate risks.

stories.title: Spices Board targets premium markets
stories.summary: The Spices Board of India has launched an initiative to expand the international footprint of Indian cardamom and other spices. A high-level consultation in New Delhi explored pathways to supply chemical-free products to premium overseas markets, focusing on global demand for value-added and pesticide-free exports.

stories.title: Regulator sets BESS project deadline
stories.summary: The Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission has directed the state power utility to commission four battery energy storage system projects by January 2027. The regulator aims to ensure peak-hour support for the state grid. The projects have a combined capacity of 235 MW and 940 MWh.

stories.title: Expert calls for fireworks reform
stories.summary: A former official from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation has urged devaswom authorities to adopt modern technology and robotics for fireworks displays. He suggested that mechanisation could prevent loss of life in the manufacturing sector, noting that current methods are increasingly out of step with global standards.

stories.title: Deep-sea fishing fleet faces regional conflict
stories.summary: Keralam-based fishing vessels report aggressive opposition from fishers in neighbouring states while operating in the Exclusive Economic Zone. Vessel owners state they are working beyond the twelve-nautical-mile state jurisdiction, while local groups are attempting to restrict access to deep-sea resources based on regional claims.

stories.title: Lancet study finds adolescent inactivity
stories.summary: A global study published in The Lancet reports that one in four adolescents worldwide does not achieve 60 minutes of physical activity on any day of the week. In 2025, approximately 240 million adolescents aged 11 to 17 reported no active days, with girls showing lower activity levels than boys.

stories.title: Centre proposes drug licence suspensions
stories.summary: The Union health ministry has proposed new rules to immediately suspend the manufacturing licences of companies whose products fail quality parameters. Under the current process, regulators issue show-cause notices before taking action. The proposed change aims to bypass this procedure to prevent substandard drugs from reaching patients.

stories.title: Health ministry targets substandard drug licences
stories.summary: The health ministry has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules of 1945 to allow for the immediate suspension of manufacturing licences for substandard medicines. The current process requires a show-cause notice, which the ministry says creates a gap during which non-compliant products may remain in circulation.

stories.title: Doctors question NEET-PG rank-based shift
stories.summary: A doctors' body has stated that changing the NEET-PG and NEET-SS from a percentile-based to a rank-based system will not resolve structural issues. Stakeholders cited exorbitant fees, compulsory bonds, and inadequate stipends as the core problems. Changing the methodology is described as a change in approach, not reform.

stories.title: Centre proposes new drug import gateways
stories.summary: The health ministry has proposed adding 10 locations to the country's authorised import network, including Noida International Airport. The move aims to allow companies to clear consignments closer to distribution centres, potentially reducing transportation costs. The ministry is currently inviting objections and suggestions on the draft amendment.

stories.title: Dental commission clarifies scope of practice
stories.summary: The National Dental Commission has issued an advisory stating that a dental degree does not qualify practitioners to perform every procedure. Dentists must restrict clinical work to areas covered by their specific qualifications and training. State councils have been asked to issue notices to prevent violations.

stories.title: Urologists assigned to emergency departments
stories.summary: Twelve government urologists who completed their M.Ch. training in 2025 are currently working as casualty medical officers. Sources report a lack of vacancies in super-speciality departments across the state. Several government medical colleges currently have no urology services despite having qualified specialists on staff in emergency roles.

stories.title: House lizards not poisonous, study suggests
stories.summary: While the common house gecko is a familiar sight in Indian homes and often associated with cultural omens, science indicates they are not poisonous. The reptiles can contaminate food, but they do not possess the toxic properties often attributed to them in local folklore.

stories.title: Thalassemia patients face supply shortages
stories.summary: The Government Medical College Hospital in Kozhikode has not resumed the free distribution of leukocyte filter sets for thalassemia patients. The devices are used to prevent adverse reactions during blood transfusions. The hospital has been without a supply of these medical devices for two years.

stories.title: ISRO mission marks recovery
stories.summary: The successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission has provided a boost to the Indian Space Research Organisation following two recent launch failures. The mission is intended to support the NavIC programme. The satellite is currently being manoeuvred into its final orbital slot to be commissioned for service.

stories.title: Proposed railway station to reach record altitude
stories.summary: A proposed railway station beneath the Tanglang La pass in Ladakh is planned at an elevation of 5,256 metres. If completed, the station would exceed the elevation of China's Tanggula station by 188 metres. The Tanggula station is currently recognised as the world's highest railway station.

stories.title: Expert team inspects Sathanur Dam
stories.summary: An expert team from the Water Resources Department conducted a structural inspection of the Sathanur Dam this Wednesday. The National Dam Safety Act 2021 requires such checks at least once a decade to enhance facility safety. The dam is now being assessed for potential structural and operational corrections.

stories.title: Hospital claims robot-assisted knee surgery speeds recovery
stories.summary: Naruvi Hospitals says its American-made CORI robot allows patients to recover from knee replacement surgery in one month instead of the traditional three. Chairman G.V. Sampath stated the technology also significantly reduces pain. The hospital is currently marketing the procedure as a cost-effective option for remote patients.

stories.title: Train strikes tiger near Shencottai
stories.summary: A tiger aged 4 to 5 years was killed by the Palaruvi Express near the Shencottai railway section early Wednesday morning. Forest officials found the carcass on the tracks with head injuries after the incident was reported at 3 a.m. The animal was crossing the ghat section.

stories.title: Second tiger death reported on rail route
stories.summary: A tiger aged 6 to 7 years was struck and killed by the Palaruvi Express on the Kollam-Senkottai route early Wednesday. Forest officials have taken custody of the animal for a necropsy. This follows a separate report of a tiger fatality on the same railway section.

stories.title: Sweet Karam Coffee reimagines Mysore Pak
stories.summary: Chennai brand Sweet Karam Coffee is collaborating with MasterChef India judge Rakesh Raghunathan to create a limited edition Mysore Pak. The company invited consumers to submit flavour ideas, with the winning concept set to join their portfolio. The brand says the sweet is well known throughout India.

stories.title: Political discourse in Punjab
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Access to the report regarding political exchanges in Punjab is currently restricted by the server. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: CJP leader responds to funding allegations
stories.summary: Cockroach Janta Party leader Ashutosh Ranka has responded to claims from Union minister Jitendra Singh regarding alleged financial support from Pakistan. Ranka questioned why the government would negotiate with his party if such claims were true. The exchange continued with further social media posts from party leadership.

stories.title: PM Modi suggests rest for Sharad Pawar
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi spoke to Sharad Pawar following the politician's discharge from a Pune hospital. An aide reported that the Prime Minister advised Pawar to rest, assuring him that Supriya Sule and others would manage national affairs. Pawar thanked the Prime Minister and confirmed he is resting.
